title: A Detention for the Mixtape
premise: Freya Amberdale, a nonbinary baker's kid at Marsh Hollow High, bakes feelings into bread and counts the days to graduation like a sentence. Cleaning out their late grandmother's recipe box, they find cards with instructions that aren't for food—spells that bake emotion, memory, and luck into whatever comes out of the oven. When Freya's bread accidentally makes the whole cafeteria weep with borrowed grief, the school's golden-boy student council president, Cass Mercer, realizes what they can do and offers protection in exchange for baked influence—first small favors, then rigged elections, then something darker. As Cass's demands corrupt the magic and Freya's loaves begin carrying Cass's cruelty back into their own hands, Freya must choose between the invisible safety they've always craved and the found family of misfits who've tasted their truth. In the end, Freya burns the recipe box's binding card in the school ovens, breaking the inheritance rather than wielding it, and serves graduation-day bread that holds nothing but their own unhidden self.
about_author: Sable Kavanagh is a former line cook who writes stories about teenagers, small towns, and the magic hidden in ordinary labor. They live above a bakery they refuse to name, and claim every loaf they've ever ruined taught them more than any workshop.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Opening in the Amberdale bakery before dawn: Freya kneads anxiety into sourdough and counts down to graduation. Establish their invisibility at school and grief over Grandma Wren's recent death. Beat: quiet longing to be seen without being exposed.

chapters.title: The Box That Isn't a Box
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Sorting Grandma Wren's kitchen, Freya finds a recipe box where cards read 'For Courage, fold thrice' and 'For Forgetting, bake at grief's temperature.' They assume it's a joke—until a test loaf makes their mother laugh for the first time in months. Beat: wonder shadowed by suspicion.

chapters.title: Cafeteria Cascade
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya brings an experimental grief loaf to school; the entire cafeteria weeps in shared mourning. Detention. Cass Mercer, watching from the back, doesn't cry—and that's what frightens Freya. Beat: exposure, the exact thing Freya feared, arriving all at once.

chapters.title: Detention Is Where the Deals Happen
chapters.summary: Cass's POV. Cass confronts Freya in detention, revealing they've seen magic before—their own family's, long gone. They offer to keep Freya's secret in exchange for 'a little help' with the student council election. Beat: the predator's smile disguised as friendship.

chapters.title: The Misfit Table
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Detention regulars—Priya the arson-adjacent chemist, Dez the mute drummer, Mr. Okafor the burned-out teacher supervising—become Freya's accidental found family. Priya guesses the bread's secret immediately. Beat: warmth Freya didn't ask for and can't refuse.

chapters.title: A Loaf for Winning
chapters.summary: Cass's POV. Cass collects a 'confidence' loaf and wins the debate for council presidency, but the magic curdles: his opponent publicly humiliates herself instead. Cass tells himself it's fine. Beat: the first taste of corruption rationalized as necessity.

chapters.title: Grandma Wren's Warning Card
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya finds a card in Wren's handwriting that isn't a recipe: 'The oven remembers what you feed it. Never bake what you wouldn't eat yourself.' Their mother admits Wren gave up magic after it 'took someone.' Beat: inheritance reframed as warning.

chapters.title: Small Favors, Compounding Interest
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Cass's requests escalate: a loaf to soften a teacher, one to sway the principal. Each time Freya complies, they feel less in their own hands. Dez notices Freya's hands trembling and starts drumming beside them at lunch. Beat: complicity deepening under the weight of friendship.

chapters.title: What Priya Bakes in Secret
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya has been testing recipe cards of her own—luck loaves for her scholarship interview—and they work too well. She and Freya compare notes and realize the box chooses an heir. Beat: shared wonder, shared dread; the found family becomes co-conspirators.

chapters.title: The Election Bake-Off
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Cass demands a loaf for the whole student body before the spring vote—mass influence. Freya refuses for the first time; Cass reveals he knows about Priya's cards and threatens them both. Beat: friendship revealed as leverage; the trap closing.

chapters.title: Invisible No More
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Dez, who hasn't spoken since a fire took his voice, eats one of Freya's honest loaves and speaks his first word in three years: Freya's name. The table erupts. Freya realizes what the magic is truly for. Beat: the emotional summit—magic as gift, not weapon.

chapters.title: Cass's Empty Kitchen
chapters.summary: Cass's POV. Flashback to Cass's childhood: his family's magic consumed his sister, and his parents taught him power is the only inheritance that protects. He believes he's saving Freya from a softer ruin. Beat: antagonist humanized without excused.

chapters.title: The Bread Turns
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya's loaves begin carrying Cass's cruelty back to them—strangers flinch, their mother goes cold, the bakery's regulars stop coming. The oven is remembering what Freya fed it. Beat: the corruption made literal and personal.

chapters.title: Burnt Offerings
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya's luck reverses catastrophically—her scholarship revoked on a technicality she can't fight. She confronts Freya: the magic takes back what it gives, with interest. Beat: the cost arrives for everyone; the family fractures under fear.

chapters.title: Mr. Okafor's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Mr. Okafor reveals he knew Wren; she baked him a forgiveness loaf decades ago and it kept him at a school he should have left. 'The cards don't make you powerful,' he says. 'They make you a kitchen other people cook in.' Beat: the mentor's truth that reframes everything.

chapters.title: The Binding Card
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya discovers the box's final card: a binding that passes the whole inheritance to one heir—unless it's destroyed by the heir's own hand in the fire it was born from. Whoever holds the box when graduation comes keeps it forever. Beat: the mechanism of the climax revealed; the clock starts.

chapters.title: Cass Makes His Move
chapters.summary: Cass's POV. Cass steals the box the night before graduation, planning to bake a loaf for the entire town at the commencement ceremony—permanent influence, permanent safety. He tells himself it's mercy. Beat: the antagonist commits fully; stakes become civic, not personal.

chapters.title: The Misfit Table Rises
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Dez, Priya, and Freya plan to take the box back—Dez speaks a full sentence for the first time to argue the plan. Priya builds a chemical counter to the ceremony's ovens. Beat: the found family chooses each other over safety.

chapters.title: Commencement Eve
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya confronts Cass alone in the school kitchen. He offers to share the inheritance; Freya sees the scared boy under the ambition and almost says yes. They refuse: 'You don't heal a hunger by feeding it.' Beat: the thematic choice stated and paid for with the friendship's death.

chapters.title: The Oven War
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At the ceremony, Cass begins the town-wide bake. Freya, Priya, and Dez sabotage the ovens; in the chaos Freya seizes the binding card and holds it over the open flame as Cass begs. Beat: the climax—Freya must burn the inheritance or claim it.

chapters.title: What the Fire Keeps
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya burns the card. The magic leaves the world gently, like steam; Cass collapses into ordinary boyhood, and Freya chooses not to hate him. The school smells only of bread. Beat: release—power refused, self chosen.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya bakes one final loaf with no magic in it at all—just flour, grief, and hope—and serves it at the misfit table. Their mother reads Wren's last plain recipe aloud. Freya walks the stage unhidden. Beat: resolution—inheritance transformed into memory, family, and an unhidden name.
